title: CBC × social media: amplification, stings, and online pile-on pattern — OSINT investigation
legal_standard: FACT = primary or on-record confirmation (CBC, Heritage, named subjects who went public, contemporaneous reporting). ALLEGATION = third-party claims under verification. INFERENCE = pattern hypothesis. Do not treat social posts alone as legal proof of harassment. No doxxing of private individuals; only public figures / public handles / institutional accounts.

thesis.short: An active social pattern links CBC productions and news framing to online individuals and activist networks who supply quotes, moral pressure, and pile-on energy — while targets experience coordinated reputational attack across X, Facebook, and Bluesky. The May 2026 CBC-linked 'sting' / prank-interview project is a primary FACT anchor; broader scrape queues map the recurring social→broadcast loop.
thesis.5gw_link: In 5GW, the cognitive battlespace includes (1) institutional amplifiers (CBC) and (2) distributed social enforcers. Using online personalities in stories while the same networks harass targets is a hybrid influence pattern — not classic one-way broadcast propaganda.

primary_case_anchor.name: CBC-linked prank / sting production targeting residential-school narrative critics (May 2026)
primary_case_anchor.summary: Frances Widdowson, Lindsay Shepherd, and others publicly described being deceived into interviews by producers using fake production-company personas. CBC confirmed involvement in the project (Counting Coup / Northland Tales class reporting) as a CBC Entertainment + APTN production; Canadian Heritage funding routed via Indigenous Screen Office grant class (~$6.3M ISO funding reporting). Yes Men / Igor Vamos named in secondary reporting as operative. Targets alleged continued recording after 'cameras off', false identities, and theatrical setup intended to smear.

primary_case_anchor.social_spillover_inference: After public exposure, secondary harassment and counter-harassment floods X/Facebook threads; scrape queues track amplifiers who convert broadcast frame into online pile-on (INFERENCE until graph measured).

steps.label: Scout
steps.description: Online activists / influencers identify targets (critics of MAID, residential-school narrative, immigration capacity, CBC funding).

steps.label: Capture / quote
steps.description: CBC or CBC-linked production solicits interviews, uses social clips, or collaborates with activist sources for 'human interest' or 'extremism' frames.

steps.label: Institutional amplify
steps.description: National broadcast/digital story grants legitimacy and reach (taxpayer-funded channels).

steps.label: Social enforcement
steps.description: Same networks (or parallel) swarm targets on X, Facebook, Bluesky — harassment, reputation destruction, employer pressure — while story remains searchable proof of 'legitimacy'.

steps.label: Feedback
steps.description: Pile-on content becomes further 'evidence' for follow-up stories or silence of dissent.

scrape_schedule.pipeline: PRISM mesh task → worker → JSONL → registry merge → site page refresh

open_questions: Full credit list and contracts for Counting Coup / Northland Tales (ATIP Canadian Heritage + ISO).
Graph: which social accounts first amplified CBC frames against each named target within 48h of story drop.
Recurrence count: CBC stories that both (a) feature activist social sources and (b) precede measurable harassment spikes against named subjects.
Cross-platform bot/coordination signals (identical copy, synchronized posts).
